title: The lost book
goals: Keep the book in a variable with a name of your own, neither `book` nor `treasure`.
goals_short: Keep the book in a variable with a name of your own.
starting_code:
# Find the book with `find_nearest` and the word "book", and keep it in a variable with a name you invent, neither `book` nor `treasure`.

# Make it glow with `reveal`.

# Walk to it: go right along the corridor to the side passage, up into the hall, left along it to its end, and one step down, beside the pile.

# Pick it up with `pick_up`.
hints: The line has the shape of my line with `treasure`, but with your own variable in its place.
`reveal` is a method of the book: that same variable of yours goes before the dot.
Walk: go right along the corridor to the side passage, up into the hall, left along it to its end, and one step down. Beside the pile of books, use `pick_up`.
intro: Eldra lost a book long ago. It lies half hidden beside the pile of old books in the corner, at the end of the aisle between the two big bookcases; you reach it from the end of the hall, just above it. Find it and keep it in a variable, make it glow, walk to it, and pick it up.
outro: You have it! Eldra waits at the other end of the hall, and she will be so glad to see it again.
learned: Now you know that the name of a variable is yours to choose, and that the thing a method gives back is used with the variable you kept it in.
